newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia okays sale rules for Ventspils terminal.
newsitem.headline: Latvia okays sale rules for Ventspils terminal.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency on Wednesday said it had approved the rules for the sale of major oil terminal Ventspils Nafta and pipeline operator Lasam and said it was not looking for a major strategic investor.
The agency said in a statement that the board approved the rules at a meeting on April 29.
The terminal is one of the main outlets for Russian crude and there has been much speculation that Russian oil firms YUKOS and LUKoil LKOH.RTS want to buy a chunk of the company.
But agency general director Janis Naglis said the sale was pitched at attracting as many investors as possible.
"There is no quota of Ventspils Nafta shares set aside for a strategic investor," Naglis told a news conference.
"Ventpils Nafta does not need a strategic investor to secure its development," he added.
"The company has been managed convincingly and with precision, showing the highest return on capital among the state companies," he said.
The rules drawn up by the agency include a four-stage process that would see the merger of Ventspils with Lasam and a privatisation to leave the state with 26 percent.
The capital of the company was planned to rise to 200 million lats from 30 million lats with the first public offers taking place in July.
All investors can take part in share auctions, either in the public offer for vouchers or the seven percent stake to be placed abroad, Naglis said.
He said that a company to carry out the international offer of Ventspils shares will be chosen in mid-May.
